Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: 6 weeks of fatigue and diffuse myalgias beginning a couple of weeks after return from U.S. travel; transient calf rash mid–late Feb; possible sore throat/fever at onset; no focal infection symptoms; no joint swelling or neurologic deficits. Past history of asthma and hay fever. Alcohol occasional; smoking not recorded.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx and transcript):
  - Lyme disease (early localized/disseminated) – High likelihood: Outdoor exposure in the U.S. with leg skin exposure; transient calf rash timing consistent with erythema migrans; subsequent fatigue/myalgias/headaches.
  - Post-viral illness/post-viral fatigue – Moderate likelihood: Sore throat and feeling feverish at onset with persistent fatigue/aches; lacks strong EBV features.
  - Hypothyroidism – Low–Moderate likelihood: Nonspecific fatigue/myalgias; needs screening though limited classic features.
  - Vitamin D deficiency – Low–Moderate likelihood: Diffuse musculoskeletal aches and fatigue; seasonal timing.
- Working diagnosis: Undifferentiated fatigue and myalgias; rule out Lyme disease.
- Plan: Proceed with blood tests including routine screening (liver, kidneys, blood count) and Lyme disease serology; treat with specific antibiotics if Lyme serology positive; arrange follow-up approximately one week after tests. (Per DDx, consideration could be given to thyroid function and vitamin D testing if initial workup is unrevealing; not recorded as ordered in this encounter.)

Management Plan

- Blood tests: Order CBC and comprehensive metabolic profile (liver/kidney), plus Lyme disease serology.
- Follow-up: Patient to book tests via support line; schedule telephone follow-up about one week after tests to review results.
- Treatment contingency: If Lyme disease test returns positive, start appropriate antibiotic therapy.
- Patient education: Discussed rationale for testing and potential Lyme disease; patient agreed to plan.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.

- CTG registration: Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Follow-up visit to review blood tests booked (telephone, ~1 week post-testing). Other preventive follow-ups: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Lyme disease (early localized/disseminated) – High: U.S. hiking with leg exposure; transient calf rash consistent with erythema migrans timing; subsequent weeks of fatigue, myalgias, mild headaches; no recalled tick bite but does not exclude Lyme.
- Post-viral illness/post-viral fatigue – Moderate: Sore throat/feverish feeling around onset with prolonged fatigue/aches; absence of focal infection.
- Hypothyroidism – Low–Moderate: Common cause of fatigue/myalgias; screening reasonable though fewer classic features.
